title: Sensitive URL pattern in web.xml (check authorization)
description: url-pattern for admin/api/actuator/console/internal — confirm AUTHORIZED via auth-constraint roles, not left UNAUTHORIZED/public.

title: Wildcard /* URL pattern in web.xml
description: Broad /* mapping — verify whether URLs are AUTHORIZED (auth-constraint) or unintentionally public.

title: HTTP TRACE method in web.xml
description: TRACE http-method declared in web.xml (CWE-693 Cross-Site Tracing).

title: CORSFilter declared in web.xml
description: CORS filter registration — ensure origin allowlist AUTHORIZES only trusted domains and url-pattern is not overly broad.

title: web.xml filter-class CORSFilter
description: Servlet/JBoss web.xml registers CORSFilter class — review origin allowlist and url-pattern.

title: Axis2 admin/service-listing surface mapped
description: The Axis2 admin console or service listing is reachable through this descriptor. Both expose deployed service metadata and, for the admin agent, hot-deployment — restrict or remove them in production. Generalized from legacy-audit patterns (regex_data/NPC-*.md, regex_data/NPG-*.md).

title: Security constraint does not require HTTPS
description: <transport-guarantee>NONE</transport-guarantee> lets this constrained resource be served over plaintext HTTP, so credentials and session cookies travel in the clear. Set CONFIDENTIAL. Generalized from legacy-audit patterns (regex_data/NPC-*.md, regex_data/NPG-*.md).

title: Known end-of-life Maven artifact
description: pom.xml declares an artifactId with a long track record of being end-of-life / unmaintained in legacy Java stacks (Struts 1.x, Axis/Axis2, Castor, JSch, Drools, Woodstox ASL, WSDL4J, xml-resolver) — confirm the actual <version> and check for a maintained replacement. Generalized from legacy-audit patterns (regex_data/NPC-*.md, regex_data/NPG-*.md).

title: SNAPSHOT version in Maven artifact
description: A -SNAPSHOT version is used for the module/parent/dependency version. Mutable, non-reproducible artifact versions are a release-hygiene / supply-chain concern if this is what actually gets built and deployed.

title: Session timeout of an hour or more
description: <session-timeout> is 60 minutes or longer, widening the window for session hijacking on shared machines. Also check it against the other descriptors in the app — a mismatch between web.xml and a secured descriptor means the longer value silently wins. Generalized from legacy-audit patterns (regex_data/NPC-*.md, regex_data/NPG-*.md).
